definitions.gloss: clothing made of light, breathable material designed to be worn in summer; the lighter version of a school or workplace uniform worn during the warm months
definitions.explanation: Refers to clothes intended to be worn in hot weather — usually thin, light-coloured, and short-sleeved. In a Japanese context, the word most often appears in two settings: (1) ordinary summer wardrobes that are taken out and put away with the seasons, and (2) the formal seasonal change of school and workplace uniforms. Japanese schools and many companies have a regulated date in May or June when employees and students switch to {夏服|なつふく}, and another date in autumn when they switch back to {冬服|ふゆふく}. This seasonal switch is called {衣替|ころもが}え.

examples.japanese: ⟦{六月|ろくがつ}→六月：00662_rokugatsu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{夏服|なつふく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Starting in June, we switch to summer uniforms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{夏服|なつふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}い→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I went to buy this year's summer clothes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{衣替|ころもが}え→衣替え：07709_koromogae⟧で、⟦クローゼット→クローゼット：04491_kuroozetto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{冬服|ふゆふく}→冬服：23084_fuyufuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{夏服|なつふく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{入|い}れ{替|か}えた→入れ替える：08227_irekaeru⟧。
examples.english: For the seasonal clothing change, I swapped the winter clothes in my closet for summer ones.

examples.japanese: ⟦{暑|あつ}く→暑い：00619_atsui⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧きた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今週|こんしゅう}→今週：00721_konshuu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{半袖|はんそで}→半袖：15518_hansode⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{夏服|なつふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}て→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧よいことになった。
examples.english: Since it has gotten hot, students at the school are allowed to wear short-sleeved summer uniforms starting this week.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧ ('summer') + ⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧ ('clothes'). The compound is fully transparent and follows the standard seasonal-clothing pattern: {春服|はるふく} ('spring clothes'), {秋服|あきふく} ('autumn clothes'), ⟦{冬服|ふゆふく}→冬服：23084_fuyufuku⟧ ('winter clothes').

USAGE:
{夏服|なつふく} can refer to ordinary summer clothing or to the lighter version of a uniform. In a school or workplace context, it almost always refers to the institution's official summer uniform — typically a short-sleeved white shirt or blouse instead of the long-sleeved winter version. The Japanese term for this seasonal switch of uniforms is ⟦{衣替|ころもが}え→衣替え：07709_koromogae⟧, traditionally done on June 1 and October 1.

In an everyday wardrobe context, {夏服|なつふく} refers to lightweight, short-sleeved clothing such as T-shirts, blouses, light skirts, and shorts that are stored separately from heavier winter clothing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夏服|なつふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧: to wear summer clothes
- {夏服|なつふく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{着替|きが}える→着替える：04603_kigaeru⟧: to change into summer clothes
- {夏服|なつふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy summer clothes
- {夏服|なつふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to take out one's summer clothes (from storage)
- {夏服|なつふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{片付|かたづ}ける→片付ける：01192_katazukeru⟧: to put summer clothes away
- {夏服|なつふく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}り{替|か}える→切り替える：04239_kirikaeru⟧: to switch to summer clothes (especially of uniforms)
- ⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{夏服|なつふく}: school summer uniform
- ⟦{制服|せいふく}→制服：03086_seifuku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{夏服|なつふく}: summer version of a uniform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{冬服|ふゆふく}→冬服：23084_fuyufuku⟧: winter clothes; winter uniform — the cold-season counterpart.
- {春服|はるふく}: spring clothes — for the cool to mild months.
- {秋服|あきふく}: autumn clothes — for the cooling months.
- {合服|あいふく}: between-season clothes — clothing for the transitional spring and autumn periods.
- ⟦{半袖|はんそで}→半袖：15518_hansode⟧: short sleeves; short-sleeved garment — refers to the sleeve length characteristic of summer clothes.
- ⟦{薄着|うすぎ}→薄着：14028_usugi⟧: light clothing — describes wearing thin or few layers, regardless of season.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The formal seasonal switch known as ⟦{衣替|ころもが}え→衣替え：07709_koromogae⟧ is a long-standing Japanese custom dating back to the Heian period. Modern schools and many companies still observe it on June 1 (switching to {夏服|なつふく}) and October 1 (switching to ⟦{冬服|ふゆふく}→冬服：23084_fuyufuku⟧). For students, this twice-yearly event is a familiar marker of the changing seasons.
